title: Copernicus Global Land NDVI 300 m, 10-daily (version 3, 2014–present)
description: The Copernicus Land Monitoring Service Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is a global 10-daily composite at about 300 m (1/336°), computed from BRDF-normalised top-of-canopy reflectances of PROBA-V (2014–2018) and Sentinel-3 OLCI (from 2019), delivered in near real time with quality flags. Version 3 reprocesses the full series from January 2014.
purpose: Near-real-time vegetation greenness monitoring at 300 m for crop-season and rangeland condition in northern Algeria, with a consistent dekadal time step suitable for anomaly-based early warning.

spatial_extent.description: Global land between 80°N and 60°S (file footprint in the CDSE index). Algeria must be subset from global files.

temporal_extent.description: January 2014 to present. In the CDSE file index, PROBA-V-based files run from 2014-01-01 to the last dekad of 2018 and Sentinel-3 OLCI-based files from 2019-01-01; the latest dekad listed in the index on 2026-11-21 was 2026-09-21 (index file updated 2026-10-01), while the metadata states a timeliness of 'within 2 days after synthesis period'.

variables.name: NDVI
variables.description: (NIR − Red)/(NIR + Red) from broad-band red and NIR reflectances

variables.name: Quality flags
variables.description: Indicates use of less-than-optimal input reflectances, sea and missing pixels

processing: NDVI is computed from global 10-daily BRDF-normalised top-of-canopy reflectances; for OLCI the two narrow red and two narrow NIR bands are averaged to broad red and NIR before computing the index. Sea pixels, out-of-range and missing reflectances are filtered, and sub-optimal inputs are flagged.
validation: The product metadata states 'Validated'; validation reports are among the CLMS technical documents, which were not read for this record.
limitations: Sensor change from PROBA-V to Sentinel-3 OLCI (between 2018 and 2019 in the file series) can introduce discontinuities in long-term anomalies; check consistency before computing trends across the transition.
NDVI over sparse vegetation and bright soils (steppe, Sahara) is dominated by soil background and is a weak indicator of biomass.
300 m pixels mix fields, orchards and bare soil in fragmented Algerian farmland.
Near-real-time dekads may be affected by persistent cloud in winter over the Tell; inspect the quality flags.
Global files are large (about 2–3.3 GB per dekad as COG); downloading via CDSE requires handling of large files or the S3/OData interfaces.

algeria_notes: Suited to dekadal monitoring of the cereal season (November–May) in the Tell and High Plateaux and of steppe green-up. For long baselines before 2014 use MODIS MOD13Q1 (existing record). Over the Sahara NDVI is near the noise level except in oases and after rare rain events.

verification.notes: Description, sensors, lineage, timeliness, CRS, resolution (1°/336), access constraints and DOI were read from the CLMS product API (metadata modified 2026-09-16). Sensor periods, file sizes, footprint and latest dekad come from the CDSE COG file index (459 files). DataCite lists the DOI (version 3.0, created 2025-11-26). The CLMS Fraction of green Vegetation Cover (FCOVER) 300 m product was not added to keep the set focused.
